theme: Swift 6 migration: language mode, strict concurrency, unchecked Sendable

terms.definition: A setting that picks which Swift version's rules the compiler follows, such as Swift 5 or Swift 6.
terms.example: Switch the target to the Swift 6 language mode.

terms.definition: A compiler setting that checks your code for data races and warns about unsafe sharing.
terms.example: Turn on strict concurrency to find data races.
terms.code:
// swift-tools-version: 6.0
import PackageDescription
let package = Package(name: "Kit", targets: [
    .target(name: "Kit", swiftSettings: [
        .enableUpcomingFeature(
            "StrictConcurrency")])])

terms.definition: A promise to the compiler that a type is safe to share, even though the compiler cannot check it.
terms.example: Use unchecked Sendable only when a lock protects the data.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to move a project step by step to Swift 6 concurrency checking: Language Mode, Strict Concurrency & Unchecked Sendable, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Language Mode - A setting that picks which Swift version's rules the compiler follows, such as Swift 5 or Swift 6.
Strict Concurrency - A compiler setting that checks your code for data races and warns about unsafe sharing.
Unchecked Sendable - A promise to the compiler that a type is safe to share, even though the compiler cannot check it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Language Mode, Strict Concurrency & Unchecked Sendable in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Language Mode, Strict Concurrency, Unchecked Sendable 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Language Mode - A setting that picks which Swift version's rules the compiler follows, such as Swift 5 or Swift 6.
한국어: Language Mode: 컴파일러가 따를 Swift 버전 규칙(Swift 5 또는 6 등)을 고르는 설정

Strict Concurrency - A compiler setting that checks your code for data races and warns about unsafe sharing.
한국어: Strict Concurrency: 데이터 레이스를 검사하고 안전하지 않은 공유에 경고하는 컴파일러 설정

Unchecked Sendable - A promise to the compiler that a type is safe to share, even though the compiler cannot check it.
한국어: Unchecked Sendable: 컴파일러가 검사할 수 없어도 타입이 공유에 안전하다고 컴파일러에게 하는 약속

dialogue.title: Fifty errors in Swift 6
dialogue.setting: A project that just switched to Swift 6

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I switched our app to the Swift 6 language mode, and now I see fifty errors.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A language mode picks which Swift version's rules the compiler follows. Swift 6 mode is much stricter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I turn on the checks step by step?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Strict concurrency is a compiler setting that checks for data races. You can enable it first as warnings.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. One error says `Cache` is not Sendable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because it has a changing property. Is anything protecting `items`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But all the tasks run one after another, I think.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do not guess. Add a lock, and then mark the class as unchecked Sendable.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is a promise to the compiler that the type is safe to share, even though the compiler cannot check it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is, so use unchecked Sendable rarely, and keep the language mode and strict concurrency settings on.
